title: 0. Executive Thesis, Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: “Risk comes from not knowing what you are doing.”
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

web_blocks.html: Azad Engineering makes precision-engineered components, mainly for aerospace, energy and oil and gas customers, and it sells most of its output abroad. Its parts are qualified with OEMs over long periods, which makes the business hard to enter and gives it a long customer relationship. The price-blind first pass found the business to be CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL, with KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH. The order book is strong, and the cash conversion is not.

Our new-capital verdict is REJECTED. On 12 November 2026 the stock closed at ₹2,468.40, against a base-case value of ₹2,373 and a probability-weighted value of about ₹2,369. The support-zone asymmetry, measured from the top of the zone, is 1.44 to 1, below the 1.5 to 1 minimum for any non-rejected call. Measured from the bottom of the zone the same ratio is about 8 to 1, so the rejection rests on the gate’s top-of-zone convention. The asymmetry gate alone would clear at about 90 times base-case profit at the zone top, but negative operating cash flow is a separate reason the verdict stays REJECTED. It is not a verdict on the company’s engineering or its order book.

The chart does not support a purchase today either. The stock is in Stage 3 by the market-facts trend filter, sits below its 20-day and 50-day averages, and is down 16.8% over one month. The timing gate reads CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. A support zone of ₹2,175.84 to ₹2,242.10 sits below the current price, with a stop at ₹2,151.41. The zone is anchored on the 13 November intraday pivot, because the 12 November ledger has no pivot level. It is a watch area, and a purchase would still need the valuation asymmetry to clear 1.5 to 1.

AZAD is not held in the Zerodha ledger as of 12 November, so the holding action is NOT_HELD and nothing needs to be sold. The next marginal rupee is retained in cash, with no allocation to the active shortlist or to outside candidates. The options status is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID, because the stock has no NSE F&O chain.

web_blocks.takeaway: The dossier says no on new capital at today’s price. The company stays on the research record, and the stock is watched for evidence that cash and valuation have caught up.

web_blocks.html: The three horizons give different answers, and each is stated separately. In the short term there is no entry, because the chart is still breaking down and the stock has not stabilised in its support zone. In the medium term the case is conditional: the 25%-plus growth guidance and the order book are real, but profit grew 6.6% in the first half against 28.6% revenue growth, and cash from operations was negative. In the long term the business has real qualification depth and long relationships, but returns on new capacity and repeat programme wins across a full cycle are not yet shown.

Several figures in this dossier rest on aggregators and press reports rather than primary filings. The gate exceptions in the spine list each disclosure, including a revenue-basis conflict, a debtor-day conflict, a stale options label and a failed market-wide scan that completed on its third attempt. None of these changes the verdict, but each limits how precisely the numbers should be read. Three research gaps, segment margin, per-part margin and top-customer share, remain unquantified.

Revisit the verdict if FY2027 full-year results show profit growth near 20% alongside positive operating cash flow, if the stock stabilises in the ₹2,175.84 to ₹2,242.10 zone and then recovers the 20-day average, or if the valuation asymmetry reaches 1.5 to 1 on updated estimates. A daily close below ₹2,151.41 closes the support setup.

book_paragraphs: Azad Engineering makes precision components that go into aerospace, energy and oil and gas equipment, and most of what it makes is sold abroad. Its parts are qualified with the customer over long periods, and that qualification is the moat. You and I should respect it. The business has a large order book of more than ₹6,500 crore and has guided to growth of about 25% a year. None of that is in dispute.

The verdict is still no. At the 12 November close of ₹2,468.40, the stock is priced above what our base case can justify. The base value is ₹2,373, and the probability-weighted value is about ₹2,369, which is 4% below the price. The support-zone asymmetry, measured from the top of the zone, is 1.44 to 1, against a 1.5 to 1 minimum. This is a close call, and we say so. It is a verdict about price and cash, not a verdict that the engineering is poor.

The chart agrees with the caution. The stock is in Stage 3, below its 20-day and 50-day averages, and it has fallen 16.8% in a month. The support zone we would watch sits between ₹2,176 and ₹2,242, and a close below ₹2,151 would end the setup. Waiting for that zone is patience with a defined exit, not a prediction that the stock will fall.

We do not hold the stock, so there is nothing to sell. The next rupee of new capital stays in cash, because no shortlist name or outside candidate clears the same hurdles in this report. Cash is a deliberate answer while cash conversion and the chart are both unresolved.

The main lesson is about cash. Reported profit has been rising, but operating cash flow was negative in FY2026 and in the first half of FY2027, while receivables, inventory and borrowings all climbed. A business can be a good manufacturer and still be a poor purchase at a multiple of 116 times trailing earnings. Keep the two judgments separate, and write down what would change each one.

Here is what we will check next. Full-year FY2027 results should show growth near 20% in profit and positive operating cash flow. Receivable days should stop lengthening. Disclosed capacity utilisation at the new facilities would show whether the expansion earns its keep. If those facts arrive, the valuation case improves. If they do not, the verdict stands.

A final caution about the evidence. Much of the financial record comes from secondary sources, and the primary filings have not been checked line by line. We have shown the conflicts and the gaps rather than smoothing them over. If you act on a later version of this view, start by confirming the numbers against the company’s own filings.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A good company is not automatically a good purchase. The price has to leave room for the business to disappoint a little and still work out. Here the room is not there yet, so the honest answer is no for now, with a clear list of what would make it yes.
